messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: fortify.sp() problem
parts:
Hi:

Spurred by a recent question regarding maps on the ggplot2 list, I
went back to the following thread

http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/3c769e24dabc78db?pli=1

and tried to reproduce the example that Tom Hooper provided then with
0.9.0. I sanitized the original csv'ed version of the Excel file to
simplify things a bit.

The zip file that contains the world borders for this example can be found at
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/57587928/TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3.zip

The sanitized csv file (meaning country name corrections) is located at
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/57587928/Total_Electricity_Net_Generation.csv

Here's the code to get to the point where the graph is to be created:

library("rgdal")
world.map <- readOGR(dsn="C:/", layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3")

# Optionally, save the map data as an R binary image ( a nested list object)
# save(world.map, file = "worldmap.Rdata")
### To read it back in later,
## library('maptools')
## gpclibPermit()
## load('worldmap.Rdata')

################ The following block works in 0.8.9 ###############
library('ggplot2') # 0.8.9
world.ggmap <- fortify(world.map, region = "NAME")

# Read in the global electricity generation data
elect.gen.tot <- read.csv(
"Total_Electricity_Net_Generation.csv", sep = ",", dec = ".")
names(elect.gen.tot) <- c("id", "y2004", "y2005", "y2006", "y2007", "y2008")

# This works in 0.8.9:
## Merge the data frames:
world.ggmape <- merge(world.ggmap, elect.gen.tot, by = "id", all = TRUE)

world.ggmape <- world.ggmape[order(world.ggmape$order), ]

## Plot the data:
world.plot <- ggplot(data = world.ggmape, aes(x = long, y = lat, group =
group))

world.plot + geom_polygon(aes(fill = y2007)) + labs(x = "Longitude", y =
"Latitude", fill = "TWh") + opts(title = "Net Electricity Generation in TWh
for 2007\nData from EIA International Energy Statistics, 2008")

####################################################################

I tried to replicate this is 0.9.0 and couldn't get the fortify.sp()
method to work on the world data:

> world.map <- readOGR(dsn="C:/Users/Dennis/Documents", layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3")
OGR data source with driver: ESRI Shapefile
Source: "C:/Users/Dennis/Documents", layer: "TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3"
with 246 features and 11 fields
Feature type: wkbPolygon with 2 dimensions
> world.ggmap <- fortify(world.map, region = "NAME")
Loading required package: rgeos
rgeos: (SVN revision 287)
GEOS runtime version: 3.3.1-CAPI-1.7.1
Polygon checking: TRUE
WARNING! if you turn polygon checking off, and polygons are
not valid in GEOS, you risk losing data as your R session may crash!

Error : package slot missing from signature for generic ‘plot’
and classes gpc.poly, ANY
cannot use with duplicate class names (the package may need to be re-installed)
Error in unionSpatialPolygons(cp, invert(polys)) :
could not find function "version_GEOS0"

# fortify.sp() indicates that it takes a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame as input:
> class(world.map)
[1] "SpatialPolygonsDataFrame"
attr(,"package")
[1] "sp"

This appears to be related to rgeos, with which I have virtually no experience.

My intention was to use this as an example for geom_map() using code
something like the following:

elec <- subset(elect.gen.tot, select = c('id', 'y2008'))
names(elec)[2] <- 'value'
> head(elec, 2)
id value
1 Bermuda 0.68432
2 Canada 632.22700

> head(world.ggmap, 2) # from the 0.8.9 data frame created
long lat order hole piece group id
1 74.91574 37.23733 1 FALSE 1 Afghanistan.1 Afghanistan
2 74.83221 37.22041 2 FALSE 1 Afghanistan.1 Afghanistan

ggplot(elec) + geom_map(aes(map_id = id), map = world.ggmap) +
expand_limits(world.ggmap)

Don't know if there's something wrong with the way I coded things or
if there's an insect to be eradicated somewhere in fortify.sp().

BTW, one of the questions I was interested in was what to do with
geom_map() when the ids, values and locations are merged into the same
file, as Tom Hooper did in his example. How would that call work?

Cheers,
Dennis
